Both Source [S1] and Source [S2] describe 'Hybrid Transparency' as a technique that splits the blending process into a 'core' (the first K fragments, typically K=16, which are depth-ordered and alpha-blended) and a 'tail' (the remaining N-K fragments, which are accumulated using order-independent blending). Both sources explicitly state that this method is used to mitigate 'popping artifacts' inherent in standard 3D Gaussian Splatting while maintaining performance.
